findings.title: Clean up browser startup on cancellation, including pre-assignment driver allocation
findings.detail: Driver start occurs outside the startup exception handler, and launch/connect cleanup only catches Exception. asyncio.CancelledError bypasses that handler. Real controlled startup probes confirm live owned driver/launcher processes after the tool has returned cancellation. The allocation-before-start-return window has no global _playwright reference, so later shutdown_browser cannot recover that resource unless the context manager/start task is retained.
findings.requested_fix: Retain startup ownership before await, handle BaseException/cancellation with shielded bounded cleanup then rethrow cancellation, and guarantee state reset even if stop is itself interrupted. Cover start allocation, launch/connect cancellation and normal EOF cleanup with isolated fixtures.
findings.resolution: Manager/start-task ownership is retained before await, startup is shielded, BaseException triggers cleanup, and nested finally clears state. Independent real launch and pre-start-return cancellation probes now show owned processes gone immediately after cancellation. Held startup gate also kills the actual driver and records cleanup incomplete instead of claiming clean success.

findings.title: Retain and clean the temporary SDK status-probe manager on cancellation/timeout
findings.detail: browser_backend_status starts a separate temporary Playwright context using async with inside asyncio.wait_for. If cancellation occurs after __aenter__ allocates a driver but before it returns, __aexit__ is never called. The context is absent from the global startup ownership added for _ensure_browser. Independent real-driver probes show it remains alive after caller cancellation and after status own five-second timeout; even shutdown_browser cannot recover it. Repeated status polling can accumulate orphan drivers.
findings.requested_fix: Give the short-lived status probe retained manager/start-task ownership and bounded cancellation/timeout cleanup equivalent to normal startup, or avoid starting a driver for this read-only probe. Add focused cancellation and natural-timeout coverage.
findings.resolution: The temporary SDK status probe now uses the same retained global manager/start-task ownership helper as browser startup and shielded finally cleanup. Independent actual-driver caller-cancellation and natural-own-timeout probes both confirm driver PID gone and globals clear. Held-gate timeout retains an explicit probeError describing timeout/incomplete protocol cleanup instead of claiming success.
